why.correct: Speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\left(x'(2)\right)^2 + \left(y'(2)\right)^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sqrt{(2 + \cos 4)^2 + (3\sin 2)^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>3.042</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3.042</annotation></semantics></math> meters per second.
options: This is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{dy}{dx}\right|</annotation></semantics></math>, the steepness of the path, not how fast the particle moves.

The speed is the length of the velocity vector, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(x'(2))^2 + (y'(2))^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This adds the two components; the speed combines them as the legs of a right triangle.
This is the square of the speed; take its square root.

items.q: What is the total distance the particle travels from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>?

why.correct: Distance traveled <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^3 \sqrt{\left(x'(t)\right)^2 + \left(y'(t)\right)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>9.482</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 9.482</annotation></semantics></math> meters.
options: This is the straight-line distance from the start to the end, the size of the displacement; the path curves.

This integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(t) + y'(t)</annotation></semantics></math>; the distance integrates the speed, the square root of the sum of squares.
The integral of the speed over the interval.
This integrates the square of the speed; the square root belongs inside the integral.

items.q: What is the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate of the particle at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>?

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^3 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^3 \left(2 + \cos\left(t^2\right)\right)dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>7.703</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 7.703</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The starting <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate plus the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, the integral of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> alone; the particle starts at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
This subtracts the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> from the start; the position adds it.

This adds the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, a rate, not the accumulated change.

items.q: What is the slope of the path of the particle at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.006</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.006</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.524</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.524</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.581</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.581</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.994</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.994</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{3\sin 1}{2 + \cos 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.994</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.994</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math> there.
options: This is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>, the reciprocal of the slope.

This is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>; the slope divides it by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is the speed at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the length of the velocity vector, not the slope of the path.

The slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The third-degree Maclaurin polynomial for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> is used to approximate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0.8</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{0.8}</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the approximation?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.205</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.205</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.226</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.226</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.120</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.952</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.952</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^3}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3(0.8)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 0.8</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>0.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 0.32</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mfrac><mn>0.512</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \frac{0.512}{6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>2.205</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 2.205</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The polynomial <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^3}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.8</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0.8</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{0.8}</annotation></semantics></math> itself, not the polynomial's approximation of it.

This stops at the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> term, the second-degree polynomial.

This leaves out the factorials: the coefficients are <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2!}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3!}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 1.

items.q: What is the length of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{x^3}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.653</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.653</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.664</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.664</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.333</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.333</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so the length is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 \sqrt{1 + x^4}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>3.653</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3.653</annotation></semantics></math>.
